text: TSA assumes a J-band Surface Transportation Security Specialist (TSS) will represent the agency at each meeting.  TSA uses a loaded compensation wage rate of $85.80 for the J-band TSS employee.  TSA estimates an annual time burden of 320 hours for the TSS employee (80 facility visits x 4 hours per visit).  Based on this information, TSA estimates a time burden cost of $27,456 for the J-band employee (320 hours x $85.80 compensation wage).  Additionally, TSA assumes a cost for planning and follow-up for a TSS per facility. TSA estimates that the J-band employee will spend 1.5 hours for planning each visit and following up after the visit.  TSA multiplies 120 hours (80 facilities x 1.5 hours x 4 (initial visit + 3 follow-ups)) by the loaded compensation wage rate of $85.80 to estimate an additional time burden cost of $41,183.  Finally, TSA estimates a time burden to TSA for the Cybersecurity Self-Assessment of 2 hours per self-assessment. TSA multiplies 100 Cybersecurity Self-Assessment respondents by 2 hours by the loaded compensation wage rate of $85.80 to get an hour burden cost of $17,160.  The total time burden cost is estimated to be $85,799 ($27,456 + $41,183+ $17,160).

text: For the contractor expenses, the cost to the Federal Government is estimated based on contractor costs per facility visit and an annual travel expense to the Government.  The costs for the CFSR visits include contractor support services to aid in the conduct of the security reviews and to complete the CFSR Form for each facility visited.  TSA estimates each facility visit costs approximately $5,055.37 in contractor expenses.  Given that TSA assumes 80 CFSR visits per year, TSA estimates the contractor expenses for CFSR visits will be $404,429.60 annually ($5,055.37 x 80 visits).  In addition, Federal Government travel costs for TSA personnel for the critical facility reviews are estimated to be approximately $41,000 annually.  TSA estimates a total annual contracting cost of $445,429.60 as displayed in table 3.

text: Under section 1557(b) of the 9/11 Act, TSA is required to identify the 100 most critical pipeline operators.  These TSA identified critical operators are subject to both the mandatory collection required by the TSA Security Directive 2021-01 series and the voluntary collection under the TSA Critical Facility Security Review (CFSR) Program.  Under the CFSR Program, critical pipeline operators identify their critical facilities using criteria in the TSA Pipeline Security Guidelines and provide that list of facilities to TSA.  TSA then reviews the security measures at those facilities.

text: Regarding the mandatory collection, TSA estimates that 97 entities will develop cybersecurity contingency response plans, conduct evaluations of the cybersecurity response plans by 3rd parties, and certify the results of the 3rd party cybersecurity evaluations. These are one-time burdens that will occur during the first year of this collection, and the total cost burden for these one-time tasks is $1,338,766 = 12,610 × $106.17.

text: TSA anticipates completing 20 PCSRs annually. text: A PCSR is conducted by one (1) representative from TSA; either a Senior Analyst (J Band) or a Junior Analyst (I Band).  Each review takes approximately 8 hours per employee.  Following the review, an additional 32 hours are devoted to completing the form, which is split equally between two analysts, for an annual hour burden of 800 hours.  TSA I-Band employees have an average fully-loaded wage rate of $73.95.  TSA J-Band employees have an average fully-loaded wage rate of $85.80.  TSA uses a simple average wage rate of $80.53 to estimate the hour burden costs, for an annual hour burden cost of $64,422.  Table 6 summarizes these estimates.

text: TSA developed the BASE program for certain surface modes of transportation to evaluate the status of security and emergency response procedures throughout the nation. TSA provides estimates of the hour burden costs due to these information collection activities.

text: For each PTPR assessment, two TSIs spend approximately 120 hours per site visit (60 hours per TSI): 20 hours for preparation, 80 hours of assessment activity, and 20 hours for data entry and follow-up.  For each HMC assessment, two TSIs spend approximately 80 hours per site visit (40 hours per TSI): 20 hours for preparation, 40 hours of assessment activity, 20 hours for data entry and follow-up.  TSA estimates an annual hour burden of 8,400 for PTPR assessments and 8,560 for HMC assessments, for a total annual hour burden of 16,960 hours.  TSA TSIs consist of H- and I-Band employees, with an average wage rate of $68.80.  TSA estimates an annual hour burden cost to TSA of $1,166,771, or $3,500,313 over 3 years.  Table 4 summarizes this estimate.

text: TSA moved to a stand-alone Cy-BASE information collection by going from two Cybersecurity Assessment information collections (PTPR Cybersecurity and HMC Cybersecurity) to one Cybersecurity Assessment information collection.  This resulted in a decrease in the cybersecurity respondents, going from 92 to 8 respondents, and a decrease in the public hour burden, moving from 1,122 to 62 annual hours.  The respondents to the PTPR and HMC Assessments information collections increased from 92 to 177 respondents and the burden increased from 575 to 823 annual hours.  As a result, the total respondents for the overall collection are 185 respondents and the total annual burden is 885 annual hours, decreasing from the previous 1,698 annual burden hours.

text: TSA estimates this collection applies to 457 railroad owner/operators, 115 rail transit system owner/operators, and 209 over-the-road bus (OTRB) owner/operators, for a total of 781 respondents. “Higher risk” rail road and rail transit owner/operators within the 781 respondents will be required to provide cybersecurity coordinator information, complete a Cybersecurity Contingency Plan, and report cybersecurity incidents.  Although the collections are voluntary for some respondents, burden calculations assume all of the respondents will do all of the collections. text: TSA estimates this collection applies to 457 railroad Owner/Operators, 115 rail transit system Owner/Operators, and 209 OTRB Owner/Operators, for a total of 781 respondents.  “Higher risk” railroad and rail transit Owner/Operators within the 781 respondents are required to provide Cybersecurity Coordinator information, complete a Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan, complete and submit to TSA a Cybersecurity Vulnerability Assessment, and report cybersecurity incidents to CISA.  Although the collections are voluntary for some respondents, burden calculations assume all of the respondents will do all of the collections.  TSA assumes these tasks will be performed by the cybersecurity coordinator, applies a fully-loaded wage rate of $109.59 for railroad cybersecurity coordinators, and $97.44 for rail transit system and for OTRB cybersecurity coordinators.

text: TSA estimates this collection applies to 457 railroad Owner/Operators, 115 rail transit system Owner/Operators, and 209 OTRB Owner/Operators, for a total of 781 respondents.   Higher-risk railroad and rail transit Owner/Operators within the 781 respondents are required to provide Cybersecurity Coordinator information, complete a Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan, complete and submit to TSA a Cybersecurity Vulnerability Assessment, and report cybersecurity incidents to CISA.  Although the collections are voluntary for some respondents, burden calculations assume all of the respondents will do all of the collections.  TSA assumes these tasks will be performed by the cybersecurity coordinator, applies a fully-loaded wage rate of $109.59 for railroad cybersecurity coordinators, and $97.44 for rail transit system and for OTRB cybersecurity coordinators.

text: To calculate the costs associated with this time burden, TSA uses a blended hourly wage rate of $62.04 based on one cybersecurity manager and four cybersecurity analysts.   TSA accounts for employer-provided benefits (non-salary compensation), by multiplying the blended hourly wage rate of $62.04 by a compensation load factor of 1.46993.  This load factor was calculated by dividing the average total hourly compensation rate for transportation industry workers by the average hourly wages and salary rate.  The resulting loaded wage rate equates to $91.19 per hour ($62.04 × 1.46993).  When combined with the estimated time burden, it results in an annual Cybersecurity Implementation Plan update time burden cost of $46,507 (510 hours × $91.19).

text: To estimate how many new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to be appointed each year, TSA first estimates the number of existing coordinators and alternates.  TSA accomplishes this by multiplying the number of Owner/Operators for each mode by 2 which results in 898 coordinators for freight rail (449 × 2), 484 for passenger rail (242 × 2), and 144 for OTRB (72 × 2).  TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) turnover rates to estimate that approximately 4 percent of the current population of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate Cybersecurity Coordinators will separate from their positions and require replacement each year.  In addition, TSA estimates that approximately 9 percent of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to submit updated contact information each year.  This results in approximately 13percent of Owner/Operators having to submit new or updated Cybersecurity Coordinator designations in a given year (4% due to turnover + 9% due to updated contact information).  Applying this percentage to the population of covered Owner/Operators results in 117 new Cybersecurity Coordinators per year for freight rail operators (898 Owner/Operators × 13%), 63 for passenger rail (484 Owner/Operators × 13%), and 19 for OTRB (144 Owner/Operators × 13%).  Table 2 presents the annual hour cost burden associated with the designation of new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternates due to employee turnover.

text: Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan and Update: All 67 Owner/Operators identified as high risk and thus subject to this requirement have developed their initial Cybersecurity Incident Response Plans and submitted them to TSA.  This population consists of 62 freight rail Owner/Operators and five rail transit system Owner/Operators.  Owner/Operators are also required to maintain up-to-date Cybersecurity Incident Response Plans, which may necessitate periodic updates.  TSA estimates that each update requires 20 hours to complete.  TSA SMEs estimate that, although the exact number may vary each year, approximately 15 percent of the Owner/Operators will need to update their plans annually.  Accordingly, TSA estimates that approximately nine freight rail Owner/Operators (62 × 15%) and one rail transit and OTRB Owner/Operators (5 × 15%) will update their Cybersecurity Incident Response Plans each year.  Therefore, the total annual time burden equates to 180 hours for freight rail Owner/Operators (9 × 20 hours) and 20 hours for rail transit Owner/Operators (1 × 20 hours), resulting in a combined total burden of 200 hours each year.

text: TSA calculates the J-band wage using the GS-14 step 5 salary for Washington, D.C. ($161,486).  To determine loaded annual salaries, TSA uses internal data to estimate costs for awards, bonuses, personnel benefits, and transit benefits, which totaled $55,926 for J-band employees.  This results in an annual salary of $217,412 for J-band employees ($161,486 + $55,926).  Dividing this figure by 2,087 annual hours yields hourly rates of $104.17.  See: “Salary Table 2025-DCB,” January 2025 (Retrieved May 2026), https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/salaries-wages/salary-tables/pdf/2025/DCB.pdf.

text: TSA assumes each new Cybersecurity Implementation Plan would be reviewed by two I-band employees (12 hours each) and one J-band supervisor (12 hours), totaling 36 hours.  TSA uses hourly rates of $88.39 (I-band) and $104.17 (J-band).  Therefore, each review is expected to cost $3,371 ((24 hours × $88.39) + (12 hours × $104.17)).  The I-band rate is based on the 2025 GS-13 step 5 annual salary for Washington, D.C. ($136,658), plus $47,807 for awards, bonuses, and benefits, totaling $184,465, divided by 2,087 hours.  Source: “Salary Table 2025-DCB,” Jan. 2025 (retrieved May 2026), https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/salaries-wages/salary-tables/pdf/2025/DCB.pdf.

text: To calculate the hourly H-band wage, TSA uses the 2025 annual salary for a GS-12 step 5 employee in the Washington D.C. area (equivalent to the H-band level), which is $114,923 per year.  TSA uses internal data to estimate the values of awards, bonuses, personnel benefits, and transit benefits, which are approximately $43,563 per year for an H-band employee.  This results in a loaded annual H-band salary of $158,486 ($114,923 + $43,563).  Dividing the loaded annual salary by 2,087 hours worked per year results in an hourly loaded wage rate of $75.94.  See: “Salary Table 2025-DCB,” January 2025 (Retrieved May 2026), https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/salaries-wages/salary-tables/pdf/2025/DCB.pdf.
